newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bid date for Mexico's refinery expansion delayed.
newsitem.headline: Bid date for Mexico's refinery expansion delayed.

text.p: Mexico has postponed the due date for bids for an $1.2 billion refinery expansion until the end August, the director general of the state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said here Thursday.

Director General Adrian Lajous told reporters that the decision to postpone the deadline date for bids for the expansion at the country's Cadereyta refinery was due to the size and complexity of the project.

Lajous stopped short of naming companies interested in the mammoth construction project. "I decline to give names now because I am not sure if the companies will make offers," he said here after inaugurating a new natural gas plant at the Cactus natural gas processing plant in the state of Chiapas.
At least 10 different companies have already registered bids for the Cadereyta project, informed sources have said.

Lajous confirmed there was a lot of interest in the project. He said one of main priorites for the project would be to process more fuel oil into natural gas and to reduce the northern area demand for fuel oil.
